provenance.dataset: Petroleum spot prices (series RWTC and RBRTE)
provenance.cadence: Each business day, roughly a two business day publication lag.
provenance.reliability: Primary source. EIA is the originator; FRED merely republishes these same two series as DCOILWTICO and DCOILBRENTEU.
provenance.caveat: These are SPOT prices, not front-month futures. Spot and the futures screen you see on CNBC can differ by a dollar or more, and spot publishes with a lag while futures are live. Do not use this to time anything intraday.
provenance.lag_note: This source publishes about 6 days behind real time, so an observation that old is normal, not a broken feed. For same-session crude you would need a front-month futures feed, which is licensed.
provenance.quality_meaning: Fetched from the originating source. This is a real observation.

impact.meaning: A RISE in this series pushes mortgage rates UP. A fall pushes them DOWN.

chains.chain: WTI crude (US benchmark) → ↑ Inflation expectations → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: WTI is the US refinery input, so it drives the gasoline line in headline CPI within two to four weeks.
The 10Y is a real yield plus an inflation expectation. Expectations move the nominal.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.
